description:
Hear ye, hear ye! We are Astrobyte, a group of software engineering and computer science students with a love for wonderful storytelling in science. 

Today we have created DoppelGrund, a search engine that aids space mission teams find new analog sites used as training grounds on Earth. It identifies never-before-seen locations using NASA data, scoring Earth against Moon and Mars targets in real measured units, and showing exactly where each match falls short
summary: Every world has a double, and DoppelGrund finds it on Earth. Before we build bases on the Moon or set foot on Mars, space mission teams need somewhere on Earth to practice, but choosing those places still comes down largely to expert opinion. The data that could settle it is scattered across space agencies and archives, in different formats, resolutions and units, so it has never been compared side by side. DoppelGrund harmonises 16 open datasets from NASA, USGS, ESA/Copernicus and research institutions into one common set of physical traits for the Moon, Mars and Earth. Pick a landmark on either world and it searches Earth for its closest matches by measurement, not by looks, scoring terrain, temperature, cold and ice, surface composition and subsurface features. Every match gets an overall score plus a score for each trait, so well-known analog sites sit beside strong candidates nobody has studied yet. Explore them on paired 3D globes and see exactly where each one holds up and where it breaks down. A twin gives you somewhere to train. Knowing how it differs from the real thing is what makes exploration possible.
details:
DoppelGrund

Every alien landscape has an Earthly twin. DoppeGrund finds it.

We harmonise scattered data from the Moon, Mars and Earth into one common language, so they can finally be compared like for like.

The problem

Preparing for future lunar and Martian missions requires Earth-based locations that resemble extraterrestrial environments. These locations, known as planetary analogs, help researchers study terrain, test equipment and understand environmental challenges before going beyond Earth.

But finding suitable analogs isn’t easy. The data that could answer the question exists, but it sits in separate archives, collected by different instruments on different worlds, in different formats, resolutions and units. Because these datasets were never put side by side, many existing sites were selected through visual resemblance or individual field studies rather than systematic, planet-wide comparisons.

DoppelGrund changes how we search for them.

DoppelGrund is an interactive planetary analog discovery platform built on a data harmonisation pipeline. It brings 16 datasets from NASA, USGS, ESA/Copernicus and university research onto one common footing, five physical traits in shared, real units for the Moon, Mars and Earth. With everything comparable, it matches selected Moon and Mars landmarks against landscapes across Earth by measurement, not appearance.

https://acrobat.adobe.com/id/urn:aaid:sc:AP:95b3622d-b63a-4088-b6da-c78166debd31

How to use DoppelGrund

Finding Earth's closest planetary twin is just a few steps away!

1. Choose Your World

Start with a short introduction from our mascot, Doppel, or skip straight ahead. Choose whether you want to explore the Moon or Mars.

2. Select a Landmark

Choose from 13 planetary landmarks: 11 on the Moon and 2 on Mars (Jezero and Gale Craters) or a custom coordinate. DoppelGrund loads the available scientific measurements for your selected location.

3. Choose Your Mission Focus

Decide what matters most to your comparison. Choose a preset (Balanced, Landing & Mobility, Cold Regions & Volatiles, or Geology & Minerals) or customise the five trait weights yourself:

  • Terrain
  • Thermal
  • Cold & Ice
  • Rock Composition
  • Subsurface Features

DoppelGrund then compares your selected landmark against sampled locations across Earth.

4. Explore the Map and 3D Globes

Discover Earth's most promising matches on the interactive map. Switch between overall similarity, individual traits and distance from documented analog sites. Explore the paired 3D globes to see how the landscapes compare.

5. Discover the Top 50 Matches

Browse the ranked shortlist of Earth locations, with an overall similarity score and individual scores for all five traits.

6. Investigate a Match

Select any location to open its detailed scorecard. Compare measurements, examine physical differences and see which scientific datasets support each result.

7. Swap to 2D Map

Switch between 3D and 2D map rendering for different views of the planet

What makes it different?

DoppelGrund goes beyond finding similar-looking landscapes. Its edge is the data.

  • Harmonised data across three worlds: The Moon, Mars and Earth are observed by different missions in different formats and resolutions. We convert them into the same five traits in real units, so an Earth location and a lunar crater can finally be compared directly.
  • Multi-source evidence: 16 datasets from NASA, USGS, ESA/Copernicus and universities, combined instead of relying on a single source. Every result shows the datasets behind it.
  • Evidence-based matching: Compares physical measurements rather than images.
  • Transparent results: Shows the differences between Earth and planetary locations in real units, including what Earth can never reproduce.
  • Discovery of overlooked sites: Highlights potential analog locations beyond already documented research sites.
  • Mission-specific comparisons: Lets users prioritise different environmental characteristics.
  • Stability testing: Tests whether leading matches remain consistent across 500 perturbed rankings.

Significance

The best location for testing rover mobility may not be the best location for studying cold environments or geological composition.

By bringing planetary and Earth observation datasets together, DoppelGrund helps researchers explore potential analog sites, identify promising locations for further investigation and make more informed decisions before committing to fieldwork.

It also makes planetary science more accessible, allowing students, educators and the public to explore the surprising connections between Earth, the Moon and Mars.

Built with open science

DoppelGrund’s strength is its data, it harmonises publicly available datasets from NASA, USGS, ESA/Copernicus and university research into one comparable framework.

The current release is a proof of concept using sampled locations and available datasets. Some measurements remain incomplete, and similarity scores indicate scientific resemblance, not guaranteed suitability for mission operations. Earth cannot reproduce the gravity, atmosphere or radiation conditions of other worlds.

Technology Stack

  • Languages: Python, TypeScript
  • Data pipeline: Google Earth Engine, numpy, pandas, scipy, rasterio, geopandas, H3
  • Analysis and ML: scikit-learn (PCA, GMM, HDBSCAN)
  • Data format: Parquet, JSON, binary arrays
  • Frontend: Vue 3, Vite, Pinia, Web Workers
  • Maps and globes: deck.gl, three.js, three-globe, h3-js
  • Testing and CI: pytest, Vitest, ruff, ESLint, GitHub Actions
  • Hosting: static site on Vercel; no backend, no GPU, no neural networks

Limitations

  • Sampled and coarse: We scored about 20,000 of 81,772 Earth land hexagons (1 in 4), using 470 m elevation and MODIS thermal alone. Each hexagon covers about 1,770 km², so small features like a single crater can be missed.
  • Data gaps: Mars temperature and caves, Southern Hemisphere permafrost, and a full Earth lava-tube list are not yet measured. Gaps show as “not measured,” never as a hidden zero.
  • Not yet validated: Our list of documented analog sites is still short, so “novel” flags are provisional. A high score also means resemblance, not proof a site is fit for training.

Future plans

  • Full planet, finer scale: Score all 81,772 hexagons with 30 m elevation and fused MODIS thermal, then re-score top matches to find the exact spot inside each.
  • Fill the gaps: Add Mars temperature, a vetted Mars cave catalogue, a larger lava-tube list, and more Moon and Mars targets.
  • Scalability: Scale to more device view to increase accessibility
